text:
Anya K: Quick follow-up on the edge proxy lifecycle change — thinking about adaptive connection handoff for long-lived streaming requests. TL;DR: can we avoid forced reconnects when we drain a node by transferring in-flight streams to another node?

Brian C: Short answer: possible but messy. We need to transfer the in-memory KV cache and resume tokens. What's the handoff surface we want to define?

Devon: We tried a tokenized resume approach before; major gotcha was sequence numbers and memory ownership. If you hand off, either the new node needs the exact KV snapshot or the client needs to present a resume token that allows rehydration without duplication.

Celeste: What about a frontdoor-based resume choreo: client reconnects with resume token, frontdoor routes to new upstream that can replay from token. Simpler than moving live state between nodes.

Anya K: Agree it's simpler, but reconnects add a visible hiccup and can break streaming semantics for low-latency interactive flows. For <100ms p95 targets, reconnect isn't great.

Brian C: Transparent transfer would require either shared low-latency state (bad perf) or a fast node->node state shipment. Maybe we snapshot a delta and stream it to the target node during drain? Then do a short atomic swap window.

Devon: Snapshot shipping is plausible. Sequence: 1) source quiesces new writes for stream ID, 2) produce compact delta, 3) push to target, 4) target warms cache, 5) switch ownership. But we need guarantees around exactly-once token consumption.

Celeste: Also we must preserve trace/span IDs and client perceived connection ID if we want transparent handoff. Otherwise many clients will treat as reconnect.

Anya K: Proposal (hybrid): default = resume-token reconnect via frontdoor (low complexity). Opt-in per-route flag = "state_handoff" that enables node->node delta shipping + warm swap for ultra-low-latency routes. Include strict fallback: if handoff fails within X ms, fall back to resume-token reconnect.

Brian C: Let's sketch an API surface for the handoff orchestration: HandoffStart(stream_id, target_node, snapshot_uri?, resume_window_ms). HandoffAck(stream_id, status, applied_seq). We need schema for the snapshot bundle (kvcache delta, last_seq, checksums).

Devon: Minimal handshake proto (pseudo):
```
message HandoffStart {
  string stream_id = 1;
  string target = 2;
  int64 last_seq = 3;
  string snapshot_url = 4;
  int32 fallback_ms = 5;
}
```
We should keep it tiny — avoid shipping full model context.

Celeste: Observability: ensure we mark traces with handoff.* spans and emit events: handoff.start, handoff.snapshot_uploaded, handoff.swap, handoff.complete, handoff.fallback. That'll make postmortems easier.

DeployBot: Pipeline: edge-proxy/handoff-refactor queued; tests: unit + integration. CI status: queued.

Devon: In terms of correctness, duplicates are the hardest problem. Consider idempotent token consumption and a short overlap window where both nodes accept requests but only one can commit to the store. Something like a lease token that moves atomically via a coordination service (etcd/consul).

Brian C: Right — atomic lease move + checksumed snapshot. If checksum mismatch, reject handoff and fall back. We need rate-limited shipping to avoid saturating network during mass drains.

Anya K: Operational controls: per-cluster handoff budget, per-tenant opt-in, telemetry knobs. Also a canary mode where we only enable handoff for <1% connections and measure p95/percent error.

Celeste: I'll write an RFC follow-up with sequence diagrams and the handoff proto + metrics to collect (handoff.latency, handoff.failure_rate, overlap_duration). Can someone add a perf target for warm handoff (p95 < 50ms added tail)?

Brian C: I'll add the state schema and perf target. Also propose a hard cap: if snapshot size > 1MB or transfer > 100ms, auto-fallback to resume-token.

Anya K: :thumbsup: thanks all. tagging @Brian C for state schema and @Devon for the proto. Let's sync tomorrow 10:30 if needed.

Celeste: Noted. I'll include a migration plan for existing routes and a toggle in Console.

Devon: Quick checklist for RFC: 1) handshake API 2) snapshot format 3) lease semantics 4) fallback policy 5) telemetry + runbook 6) perf targets.

Anya K: Perfect. Closing this thread for now — RFC draft expected EOD.
